title: Météo : 2025, le troisième été le plus chaud de l'histoire en Tarn-et-Garonne après 2022 et 2003
content: The meteorological assessment of the 2025 summer in Tarn‑et‑Garonne, covering 1 June to 31 August, shows that it was the third hottest on record for the region.  The average maximum temperature reached 29.7 °C, with the peak daily maximum on 11 August recorded at 42 °C – the third highest ever measured in the commune.  In Montauban the same day the thermometer read 41.8 °C, while in Caylus it reached 40.7 °C.  The 2023 summer, which also featured a heatwave, had a comparable average maximum of 29.7 °C.  The two previous record summers were 2022 (32 °C) and 2003 (31.9 °C), as noted by the MétéoFrance technician: 'Seules les années 2022 avec 32°C et 2003 avec 31,9°C sont au-dessus depuis le début de nos relevés à Montauban, en 1963. Il y a malgré tout une énorme différence avec ces deux valeurs-là'.  Minimum temperatures followed a similar pattern, with 2025’s average low of 17.1 °C ranking just below 2003 (18.5 °C), 2022 (17.4 °C) and 2023 (17.2 °C).  July experienced a severe drought, with only 12 mm of rainfall recorded in Montauban compared to a 60‑year average of 47 mm, according to Valéry Moutot: 'Pour la station de Montauban, on a ainsi relevé 12 mm de précipitations seulement, contre une moyenne de 47 mm sur les 60 dernières années'.  June 2025 received 55 mm, slightly below the 68 mm average, while August saw 68 mm, surpassing the 55 mm average.  Moutot cautioned against generalising these figures across the department: 'Il est néanmoins très dangereux, sur cette donnée, d'extrapoler avec l'ensemble du département, altère le météorologiste'.  Overall, the 2025 summer was described as 'bien ensoleillé' and its insolation ranked 12th among the last 35 years.

title: Août 2025, le troisième mois le plus chaud jamais enregistré en Dordogne - ici
content: In August 2025, the Dordogne department experienced its third‑hottest month on record since 1960, following August 2023 and August 2022, according to Météo France data. The average temperature was a little over 22 °C, a degree and a half above normal, as Thierry Godain, a forecaster at Météo France, noted 'ce qui est un degré et demi de plus par rapport à la normale'. A heatwave from 7 to 17 August averaged 35 °C and produced two record peaks. On 11 August every temperature record was broken: 43.5 °C in Monpazier, 42 °C in Périgueux, Bergerac, and the Eyzies, and nearly 42 °C in Montignac‑Lascaux. On 13 August temperatures never fell below 20 °C, with 23.6 °C in Bergerac, which Godain described as '23,6 degrés à Bergerac, ce qui se rapproche d’une nuit tropicale'. The month saw 260 hours of sunshine, 15 % more than normal, '15% de durée d’ensoleillement en plus que la normale'. The region remained very dry until 18 August, when thunderstorms on 19 and 20 August brought some rain. Heavy showers on 29 August raised August’s total rainfall to 63 mm, close to the usual 67 mm, with 30 mm recorded in Saint‑Martin‑de‑Fressengeas and Terrasson‑Lavilledieu and up to 50 mm in some spots.

title: Records de chaleur : pourquoi les 50 °C ne sont plus impossibles...
content: While temperatures above 40°C are common in France during the summer, it is possible that the country could reach temperatures of 50°C in the future. According to Météo France, the temperature record in France is 46°C, set in Vérargues in 2019. However, to reach 50°C, an additional 4°C would be needed. While the climate is warming rapidly, Météo France predicts that the 40°C threshold will be reached annually around 2100, and that local records of 50°C 'are possible as early as 2050' and 'probable' by the end of the century. It is therefore possible that certain departments in southern France could reach 50°C within the next 25 years. As Météo France notes, 'it is not the real temperature that is felt, but the perceived temperature, which can already reach or exceed 50°C in the south of France during heatwaves associated with humid air.'

title: Quel temps est-il prévu à La Flèche et ses environs le mercredi 27 août 2025 ?
content: On Wednesday 27 August 2025, La Flèche will experience temperatures around 20 °C with an essentially covered sky, as the forecast states, 'La Flèche connaîtra des températures avoisinant 20 degrés et un ciel essentiellement couvert.' No precipitation is expected during the day. In the morning, the sky will be clear at dawn, with temperatures starting at 13 °C and rising to 23 °C by early afternoon. Wind will begin at 20 km/h at 7 h, increasing to about 35 km/h, with gusts up to 45 km/h, from the southwest. In the afternoon, the sky remains covered, wind around 40 km/h, temperature steady at 24 °C, gusts over 50 km/h, still from the southwest. Evening wind drops to ~20 km/h between 20 h and midnight, gusts up to 65 km/h, with clouds persisting. Night temperatures fall to 16 °C, wind rises to ~30 km/h between 2 h and 5 h, gusts up to 65 km/h, clouds become denser, with light rain expected late at night. Thursday will be mild, 13–23 °C, mostly very cloudy, no severe weather.

title: Jusqu'à 14 °C de moins : une importante chute des températures attendue d'ici jeudi
content: A significant drop in temperatures is expected in France by Thursday, with a possible decrease of up to 14°C. According to La Chaîne météo, the mercury could drop to 26°C in Perpignan, 25°C in Bordeaux, and 19°C in Lyon. Météo France predicts a mostly cloudy sky across the country, with temperatures ranging from 18°C in Brest to 24°C on the Mediterranean coast. Rain is also expected in the east and south of France. By Thursday, temperatures are expected to drop to 20°C in Paris, Strasbourg, and La Rochelle, and to 19°C in the south-east. 'Sortez les parapluies' (take out your umbrellas), as showers and thunderstorms are expected to affect the country, particularly the south, on Tuesday. Temperatures will remain relatively high, however, with 28°C expected in Paris, Strasbourg, and Perpignan. By the weekend, a mostly clear sky is expected, with temperatures around 25°C.

title: Un ciel assez dégagé mais des températures toujours fraîches : la météo de ce week-end en France
content: According to Météo France, the majority of France will not see temperatures above 20 °C even in the afternoon, despite clear skies. The weekend will be calm with no precipitation. Saturday morning: western France will be fairly cloudy, the Paris region very cloudy, and dense fog will surround Auxerre and Chaumont; southern areas such as Lyon, Nice and Marseille will see sunshine. Ajaccio in Corsica will reach 22 °C, the only region above 20 °C. In the afternoon, the west will clear but not fully bright; fog will lift; temperatures may exceed 20 °C in Bordeaux, Toulouse, Montpellier and Nice. Evening: light rain will fall in Brest, and the sky will be cloudy around Nantes, Limoges, Aurillac and Perpignan. Sunday will follow a similar pattern, with 20 °C in Ajaccio. Monday will remain calm and cool, with a few showers in Cherbourg. Tuesday will bring showers in the east. The forecast notes that "Le soleil sera au rendezvous" in the south and that "le brouillard se dissipera" in the west, underscoring the expected clear but cool conditions.

title: Prévisions météo du mardi 26 août 2025 à Nantes
content:
The forecast for Nantes on Tuesday, 26 August 2025 predicts daytime temperatures between 14°C and 26°C, with a gentle south‑west wind. Morning will have some clear skies, but afternoon sunshine will be delayed by clouds and scattered showers are expected. Temperatures will range from 23°C to 26°C, with an average evening temperature of 17°C, and the night will bring a misty sky. The following day will see a slight drop in temperatures, with values between 13°C and 25°C, a light south‑west breeze, and morning temperatures around 20°C. Maxima may reach 25°C in the afternoon and minima 21°C, with the sky clearing somewhat in the evening. The weather will vary over the next days, with an improvement expected on Friday after a rainy Thursday.

Key metrics quoted in the source include: 'Il va faire 17°C en moyenne le soir.' and 'Les températures seront comprises entre 13 et 25°C.'

title: Les prévisions météorologiques du mardi 26 août 2025 à Niort et ses environs
content: On Tuesday 26 August 2025, Niort is forecast to have an average temperature of about 23 °C with predominantly cloudy skies and no severe weather. The forecast details a temperature rise from 16 °C at dawn to a high of 29 °C at 16:00, wind speeds ranging from 15 km/h at 6:00 to a maximum of 40 km/h in the late afternoon, with gusts up to 55 km/h. Wind direction is variable, shifting from northwest to south overnight. The following day, temperatures will be lower, averaging 20 °C with a maximum of 24 °C, still cloudy but with no precipitation expected. (Source: Ouest France, 26 August 2025).

title: Météo : des températures estivales attendues pour la fin de la semaine - ici
content: According to Météo France, summer‑like temperatures are expected to arrive by the end of this week. The forecast shows a gradual rise in the mercury starting on Wednesday, with the northern half of the country warming first. On Tuesday, maximum temperatures ranged from 18 to 22 °C; by Wednesday, they are projected to reach 21–25 °C, with 24 °C in Bourges and Tours and 23 °C in Nantes. The Mediterranean hinterland will also experience summer heat, with 31–33 °C expected. Thursday’s highs are forecast at 21–25 °C in Brittany and 25–29 °C in the rest of the north and the Lyon area, while Bourg‑Saint‑Maurice and Aurillac should see 26 °C. Southern regions, including the Garonne, may reach 34–35 °C. Friday’s maximum temperatures climb further to 28–32 °C in the southeast and north, 20–25 °C in Brittany, and 32–36 °C in the southwest. Saturday will maintain summer temperatures, with highs of 26–30 °C overall and about 23 °C in Brittany. The return of autumn is anticipated on Sunday, with maximum temperatures ranging from 22 to 28 °C across the west, east, and Mediterranean areas.

title: L'épisode caniculaire en déclin dimanche sur une grande partie de la ...
content: A heatwave that has been affecting a large part of France for the past 10 days is expected to decline on Sunday and focus on the southern half of the country and Brittany, with 36 departments placed on orange alert by Météo-France. Temperatures are expected to reach up to 41°C in the interior of Languedoc and Roussillon, with Perpignan and Montpellier expected to exceed 40°C. However, a cooler air mass is moving in from the north and is expected to bring temperatures down across the country. By Sunday morning, the orange alert is expected to be lifted for the departments of Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, Brittany, and Corsica. Météo-France has also placed Corsica on yellow alert for thunderstorms on Sunday. The heatwave, which began on August 8, has been particularly intense in the south of France, with many records broken. According to Météo-France, 266 weather stations recorded temperatures of 40°C or higher between August 9 and 12, a notable increase from the second half of the 20th century. The heatwave is expected to end between Monday evening and Tuesday morning.
